records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Atoms contain sub-atomic particles—electrons, protons and neutrons. This chapter develops atomic models and the quantum-mechanical description of electrons.
records.keywords: atom atomic structure electron proton neutron subatomic particles Dalton

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Cathode-ray experiments established the existence of negatively charged electrons and helped determine their charge-to-mass relationship.
records.keywords: electron cathode rays discharge tube charge mass Thomson

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Positive particles were associated with the nucleus; the neutron is electrically neutral. Together protons and neutrons account for nuclear composition.
records.keywords: proton neutron nucleus positive charge neutral particle Chadwick

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Thomson pictured the atom as positive matter with electrons embedded in it, arranged so that the atom as a whole is electrically neutral.
records.keywords: Thomson model plum pudding positive sphere electrons neutral atom

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Alpha-particle scattering showed that most of an atom is empty space and that its positive charge and most of its mass are concentrated in a very small nucleus.
records.keywords: Rutherford alpha scattering gold foil nucleus empty space atomic model

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Atomic number Z is associated with the number of protons; mass number A represents the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
records.keywords: atomic number mass number Z A protons neutrons nucleons isotope isobar

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers, whereas isobars have the same mass number but different atomic numbers.
records.keywords: isotopes isobars atomic number mass number hydrogen deuterium tritium

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Electromagnetic radiation is described by wavelength, frequency and velocity; wavelength and frequency are inversely related for radiation travelling at a fixed speed.
records.keywords: electromagnetic radiation wavelength frequency velocity spectrum c lambda nu wave

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Planck proposed that energy is emitted or absorbed in discrete quantities called quanta, with photon energy proportional to frequency: E = hν.
records.keywords: Planck quantum theory quantum photon energy h nu frequency E=hnu

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: The photoelectric effect demonstrates interaction of radiation with matter in which electrons are ejected when radiation of sufficient frequency strikes a suitable surface.
records.keywords: photoelectric effect photon electron threshold frequency Einstein kinetic energy

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Excited atoms produce characteristic line spectra rather than a continuous spectrum. Emission and absorption spectra provide information about atomic structure.
records.section: Evidence for Quantized Electronic Energy Levels: Atomic Spectra
records.keywords: atomic spectra emission absorption line spectrum continuous spectrum excited atom

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: The hydrogen line spectrum consists of series of spectral lines corresponding to transitions between quantized energy levels.
records.keywords: hydrogen spectrum Lyman Balmer Paschen Brackett Pfund Rydberg spectral series

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Bohr proposed permitted stationary orbits with quantized energies; radiation is emitted or absorbed when an electron moves between allowed energy states.
records.keywords: Bohr model stationary orbit hydrogen atom quantized energy angular momentum transition

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: For hydrogen-like species, permitted orbit radii and electron energies depend on the principal quantum number and nuclear charge; energy becomes less negative as n increases.
records.keywords: Bohr radius energy orbit n Z hydrogen like ion ground state excited state ionisation

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Bohr’s model successfully treats hydrogen-like systems but cannot adequately describe spectra and behaviour of multi-electron atoms and is incompatible with the modern probability description of electrons.
records.keywords: limitations Bohr model multi electron atom Zeeman Stark spectrum

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Matter such as an electron has wave character. The wavelength associated with a moving particle is related to its momentum by λ = h/p.
records.keywords: de Broglie matter wave wavelength momentum lambda h p dual nature electron

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: The exact position and exact momentum of a microscopic particle cannot simultaneously be specified with arbitrary precision.
records.keywords: Heisenberg uncertainty principle position momentum velocity delta x delta p

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Quantum mechanics replaces definite electron paths with wave functions and probability-based atomic orbitals describing where an electron is likely to be found.
records.keywords: quantum mechanical model Schrodinger wave function psi probability orbital electron density

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: The principal quantum number n identifies the principal shell and is related to orbital size and, to a large extent, orbital energy.
records.keywords: principal quantum number n shell K L M N size energy

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: The azimuthal quantum number l identifies a subshell and is associated with orbital shape; allowed values range from 0 to n−1.
records.keywords: azimuthal angular momentum quantum number l subshell s p d f shape

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: The magnetic quantum number ml specifies orbital orientation. For a given l it has 2l+1 permitted values, corresponding to the number of orbitals in that subshell.
records.keywords: magnetic quantum number ml orientation orbital 2l+1

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Electron spin has two possible orientations represented by ms = +1/2 or −1/2. Two electrons in one orbital must have opposite spins.
records.keywords: spin quantum number ms electron spin plus half minus half opposite spins

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: A Bohr orbit is a proposed circular path, whereas an atomic orbital is a quantum-mechanical region described by a wave function and electron probability. Orbit and orbital are not synonymous.
records.keywords: orbit orbital difference Bohr path probability region wave function

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: s orbitals are spherically symmetric, while p orbitals have directional lobes; orbital shape and orientation follow from the quantum numbers.
records.keywords: shape orbital s p d spherical dumbbell nodes radial angular probability density

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: In hydrogen the orbital energy depends on n. In multi-electron atoms orbital energy is influenced by both n and l as well as electron interactions and effective nuclear charge.
records.keywords: orbital energy n plus l rule effective nuclear charge shielding penetration degenerate

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: In the ground state, electrons occupy available orbitals in order of increasing energy, filling lower-energy orbitals before higher-energy ones.
records.keywords: Aufbau principle filling order 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d n+l

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: No two electrons in an atom can have the same set of four quantum numbers. An orbital can contain at most two electrons and they must have opposite spins.
records.keywords: Pauli exclusion principle four quantum numbers opposite spin two electrons orbital 2n2

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: For degenerate orbitals of a subshell, pairing does not begin until each orbital has first received one electron.
records.keywords: Hund rule maximum multiplicity degenerate orbitals singly occupied pairing p d f

records.subject: Chemistry
records.meaning: Electronic configuration is the distribution of electrons among atomic orbitals according to orbital energies and the Aufbau, Pauli and Hund rules.
records.keywords: electronic configuration orbital diagram electron filling hydrogen helium lithium carbon nitrogen oxygen neon

records.subject: Chemistry
records.topic: Stability of Half-filled and Completely Filled Orbitals
records.meaning: Half-filled and completely filled sets of degenerate orbitals have extra stability, associated in NCERT with symmetry and exchange energy considerations.
records.section: Stability of Completely Filled and Half Filled Subshells
records.keywords: half filled fully filled completely filled subshell stability symmetry exchange energy chromium copper
